## Overview

RLM-CA-001 describes the same-wave correlates of BAS word reading in the Byrne, MacDonald and Buckley historical cohort. At each of waves 1–4 it fits a separate between-child Beta-Binomial regression of BAS word-reading level (`basread`) on receptive vocabulary (`bpvs`), receptive grammar (`trog`), auditory digit recall (`basdig`) and verbal similarities (`bassim`), plus age and reading-group nuisance terms. The mutually adjusted result is shown beside a single-skill comparator for each predictor. The Beta-Binomial concentration takes the dispersion-scale prior shared by the Byrne families, $1/\sqrt{\kappa} \sim \mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.25)$ (2026-08-22 adjusted-family review), so the near-Binomial limit is not excluded a priori.

_Estimand: descriptive association, with no causal warrant._ The coefficient for a predictor compares children at the same wave who are alike on the model's other included variables. It does not estimate what would happen if that skill were changed. The reading-matched group was selected on reading level, so neither its nuisance coefficient nor a pooled association should be read as an unselected population contrast.

## Design

- The four waves are fitted separately. Wave 4 is an available-case, attrition-sensitive extension beyond the primary paper's audited waves 1–3; it is not automatically more informative because it is later.
- The battery is deliberately restricted to the five measures whose bounded-count denominators and instrument identities are confirmed and which have wave-1 values. BAS spelling (`basspel`), WORD comprehension (`woco`) and BAS number skills (`basnum`) remain excluded because their denominators are provisional. Source-native BAS Matrices (`basmat`) is confirmed but remains excluded because it has no wave-1 value and is not part of the paper's reported three-wave battery.
- Predictors enter as within-wave standardised Haldane-corrected logits with regularising `Normal(0, 0.3)` slopes. The adjusted and single-skill coefficients answer different questions; their difference is sensitivity to the conditioning set, not a decomposition of shared variance.
- Missing focal outcomes are excluded. Missing predictor scores are mean-imputed to zero on their within-wave standardised scale and their observed and imputed counts are reported. This pragmatic descriptive policy can bias coefficients in either direction when missingness depends on measured or unmeasured characteristics.
- Reading group is represented by two nuisance dummies rather than one numeric slope. The model does not assume that the three group codes form a linear scale, and it does not report a group effect.
- `bassim` is a verbal-similarities measure, not a complete control for general ability. Residual confounding, measurement error and collinearity remain plausible.

The extract lineage was reconciled on 2026-08-16 against the checksum-pinned 97-case SPSS source. A fresh fit can therefore clear the dataset-level input gate; any fit stored before that decision retains its original fail-closed input snapshot and must be regenerated before scientific interpretation.
